task: Revise the setup of `test_w2_76_watchdog.py::test_a_slow_rebuild_records_what_it_waits_on_and_goes_on` under DEC-956 item 1 so the slowed rebuild is the first on its tree, lowering no expectation.
status: DONE. The revised test passes, the whole folder passes (22 of 22), and commit ef26e1a15057 exists.
work_completed: The slowed rebuild now runs first on a tree no rebuild has touched. Its unslowed counterpart is the first rebuild of a twin project: the same files in the same commit, in a box of its own. After the records are judged, an unslowed rebuild of the same tree makes a second comparison. The live-record check now judges the last read taken while the slow stage runs, not the last read of the whole run. The docstring and the README's line for this test give the new setup and the reason (DEC-956 item 1).
files_changed: tests/acceptance/W2-76/test_w2_76_watchdog.py; tests/acceptance/W2-76/README.md
evidence: Commit ef26e1a15057, "W2-76: the slow-rebuild case's setup revised so the slowed rebuild is the first on its tree", with trailers Task: DAEO-tgk2 / Role: independent-test-designer / Implements: DEC-956 / Rewrite-Reason: DEC-956 item 1 / Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5. The code under test: `PYTHONPATH=/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-76/src python3 -c "import gov; print(gov.__file__)"` printed `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-76/src/gov/__init__.py`. Scratch, `du -s --inodes` / `du -sh` of the temporary folder: 8 / 24K before the runs, 17 / 52K at the end, well within the 2 GB and 100,000 budget.
tests: Whole folder `tests/acceptance/W2-76`: 22 passed in 102 s (no `-x`, `-o tmp_path_retention_policy=failed`). `test_w2_76_watchdog.py` alone: 3 passed, three runs in a row, 28 to 34 s each. Two earlier runs of my intermediate versions failed for setup reasons, both fixed (see discoveries).
discoveries: (1) The digest is taken from the record store, which holds the commits table. A twin project only gives the same digest when its commit hash is identical, so the twin is committed with fixed author and committer dates, and the test asserts the hashes match. (2) Inside the sandbox, the code index's reason in `stores` names `/tmp/gov-cbm-1000/<hash>`, a folder derived from the project's path. So the twin's `stores` differ from the slowed project's in that reason text: the twin is compared on each store's status, and the full `stores` are compared with a rebuild of the same tree. (3) Now that the sleep sits in the lexical stage (a middle stage), the watchdog rewrites the record during the later stages. One run's last live read showed the stage running as `codeintel`, so the old "last read" choice became a race. The fix: the case judges the last read whose stage running names `lexical` or `secrets`. It also requires at least one such read and at least two distinct write times within that stage (new and stricter). (4) The worktree root shows untracked character devices (`.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, `.mcp.json`, `.idea`, `.vscode` and others, device 1,3), which are the sandbox's placeholders. I did not make them and did not commit them.
risks: Choosing the last read within the slow stage, instead of the last read of the run, is my judgement and the auditor should look at it. Every part is still checked on that read, the planted gitleaks must still appear in its process list, and the stricter checks above are added. The digest and stores comparison with the same tree is now with a rebuild after the slowed one, so that rebuild is incremental. The digest comparison stays whole because the record store is reloaded in full from git on every rebuild. Outside the sandbox the code index's reason may differ, but both full-`stores` comparisons are at the same path, so this should hold there too; only the lead's run outside the sandbox can confirm it.
lessons: Before comparing across two projects, check what the digest and `stores` are made of: commit hashes and path-derived folder names make them depend on the project. In a case that polls a record, choose the read by its stage, not by its position, whenever the planted delay is not in the last stage.
proposed_decisions: none
unresolved: The lead's run outside the sandbox, where the code-graph folder is writable and the code-index stage behaves differently.
recommended_next_action: The lead runs `tests/acceptance/W2-76` outside the sandbox on this commit, then continues with DEC-956 item 2 (the lock-path override).

guard_refusals: none

- **Sandbox check (step 0):** (a) the write outside the worktree failed with `OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system`, so no file was made. (b) `git hash-object -w --stdin` and `git update-index --refresh` worked (exit 0). `GOV_ROLE` / `GOV_TICKET` were `independent-test-designer` / `DAEO-tgk2`. The top level and branch were `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-76` and `w2/W2-76`. The nightly flag was absent both times I checked.
- **Commit:** ef26e1a15057.
- **What changed in the setup and why:** The slowed rebuild now runs first on its tree. Before, it was the second rebuild of an indexed tree, so the lexical index (incremental by blob) skipped the secrets filter and the sleep landed in the code index. The unslowed comparison is now the twin's first rebuild, run after the slowed one: same commit, its own HOME, TMPDIR and tools. Two first rebuilds are compared, so neither can reuse the other's index. They are compared on the digest and on each store's status, because a store's reason may name a path-derived folder. A final unslowed rebuild of the same tree is compared on the digest and on `stores`, every field. Every original expectation is kept: `secrets_s` and `lexical_s` now each measure at least 8 s.
- **Counts:** whole folder 22 passed; the watchdog file 3 passed in each of three runs.
- **Guard read refusals (DEC-849):** 0.
- **`gov retrieve`:** used once. It answered `STORE_MISSING` (no record graph in this worktree's store), so it served no results and none had to be dropped under P-R1. Instead I read `src/gov/rebuild/command.py` and `src/gov/store/loader.py` as they stand on `w2/integrate`, through `git show` and `git grep` (allowed under DEC-820 (c)). I never read the branch's implementation files.
- **Scratch:** 8 inodes / 24K before, 17 inodes / 52K at the end.
